materials.text:
First, you must read from the Node.Ready() channel and process the updates
it contains. These steps may be performed in parallel, except as noted in step
2.

1. Write HardState, Entries, and Snapshot to persistent storage if they are
not empty. Note that when writing an Entry with Index i, any
previously-persisted entries with Index >= i must be discarded.

2. Send all Messages to the nodes named in the To field. It is important that
no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk,
and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while
entries from the same batch are being persisted). To reduce the I/O latency, an
optimization can be applied to make leader write to disk in parallel with its
followers (as explained at section 10.2.1 in Raft thesis). If any Message has type
MsgSnap, call Node.ReportSnapshot() after it has been sent (these messages may be
large).

Note: Marshalling messages is not thread-safe; it is important that you
make sure that no new entries are persisted while marshalling.
The easiest way to achieve this is to serialize the messages directly inside
your main raft loop.

3. Apply Snapshot (if any) and CommittedEntries to the state machine.
If any committed Entry has Type EntryConfChange, call Node.ApplyConfChange()
to apply it to the node. The configuration change may be cancelled at this point
by setting the NodeID field to zero before calling ApplyConfChange
(but ApplyConfChange must be called one way or the other, and the decision to cancel
must be based solely on the state machine and not external information such as
the observed health of the node).

4. Call Node.Advance() to signal readiness for the next batch of updates.
This may be done at any time after step 1, although all updates must be processed
in the order they were returned by Ready.

Second, all persisted log entries must be made available via an
implementation of the Storage interface. The provided MemoryStorage
type can be used for this (if you repopulate its state upon a
restart), or you can supply your own disk-backed implementation.

Third, when you receive a message from another node, pass it to Node.Step:

AsynchronousStorageWrites, and can be enabled using the flag on the Config
struct with the same name.

When Asynchronous Storage Writes is enabled, the responsibility of code using
the library is different from what was presented above. Users still read from
the Node.Ready() channel. However, they process the updates it contains in a
different manner. Users no longer consult the HardState, Entries, and Snapshot
fields (steps 1 and 3 above). They also no longer call Node.Advance() to
indicate that they have processed all entries in the Ready (step 4 above).
Instead, all local storage operations are also communicated through messages
present in the Ready.Message slice.

The local storage messages come in two flavors. The first flavor is log append
messages, which target a LocalAppendThread and carry Entries, HardState, and a
Snapshot. The second flavor is entry application messages, which target a
LocalApplyThread and carry CommittedEntries. Messages to the same target must be
reliably processed in order. Messages to different targets can be processed in
any order.

Each local storage message carries a slice of response messages that must
delivered after the corresponding storage write has been completed. These
responses may target the same node or may target other nodes.

With Asynchronous Storage Writes enabled, the total state machine handling loop
will look something like this:

	for {
	  select {
	  case <-s.Ticker:
	    n.Tick()

formation.explanation: Leader proposals receive term/index, append to the log and queue a persistence-delayed self acknowledgment. Peer acknowledgments update progress; tracker aggregates current voters using both majorities for joint configuration, then maybeCommit checks the current log term before advancing commitment. Acknowledgment-driven advancement broadcasts append and releases queued reads, while configuration-driven advancement broadcasts without that release.

context.explanation: Campaign transitions establish candidate term and self vote; vote eligibility uses local vote/leader context and log freshness. PreVote leaves term and vote unchanged. Step handles message terms before role handlers, with explicit pre-vote/lease exceptions and lower-term rejection. Role reset clears accumulated progress and readOnly context while preserving the committed prefix.

connection.explanation: Term dispatch prevents ordinary old responses from becoming new leader support. Persistence-delayed vote/append replies and leader self replies connect durable support to election and commit decisions. Configuration application reinterprets peer progress through a changed voter set and may itself advance commitment; established committed history constrains snapshots and subsequent log repair.

important_branches: Simple changes cannot alter more than one voter or run inside joint state; zero voters are rejected.
EnterJoint preserves the old voters as outgoing; LeaveJoint drops outgoing voters and activates staged learners. Retained peers retain progress; new peers start Match zero.
Leader admission ordinarily allows at most one unapplied configuration proposal; invalid requests become empty normal entries.
switchToConfig updates eligibility and may recompute commitment; removal/demotion steps down only when configured, and removed leaders cannot propose new entries.

important_branches: Non-singleton leader postpones requests until an entry is committed in its term. Singleton returns its committed index directly.
Safe mode records request/index, self-acknowledges and broadcasts a context heartbeat; current configured quorum acknowledgments advance the queue and produce local ReadStates or remote responses.
Lease mode returns the committed index after its admission condition. Host must correlate context and wait for state-machine application before serving reads.
Role reset clears readOnly quorum acknowledgments; pending pre-first-commit requests survive reset and may later be released with a fresh index/quorum. API allows lost requests and requires retries.
unknowns: Reachability of first current-term commit via switchToConfig without release; an unexecuted path alone does not establish a liveness violation.

Async storage append messages attach all deferred replies and a term-stamped stabilization response. Even an empty append can carry prior-state-dependent replies. Same-target reliable FIFO is a caller duty.
Async stabilization uses both current response term and entry identity; lower-term responses cannot remove unstable entries, while snapshot completion remains term-independent.
Node serializes core calls and prevents another synchronous Ready until Advance; both Node and RawNode reject unexpected network local messages and unknown-peer responses.

after.execution_owner: raft append/snapshot handlers and progress replication
after.protocol_context: Follower log prefix and leader progress
after.trigger: MsgApp, MsgSnap, rejections, heartbeat recovery and transport reports
important_branches: Follower matches previous entry identity, truncates only conflicting uncommitted suffix, and caps propagated commit by received log end. Heartbeat commit is capped at peer Match by sender.
Rejections adjust Next; heartbeat responses can unpause and send empty appends after lost in-flight messages. Missing local history triggers snapshot fetch if peer recently active.
Snapshot restore ignores obsolete indexes, refuses a recipient absent from membership, fast-forwards matching log history, otherwise restores log and configuration.
Snapshot failure and unreachable reports return progress to probing; successful snapshot or append acknowledgments resume replication.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Repairs eligible durable support while guarding established committed prefixes.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Snapshot acceptance is on follower paths; pending snapshots prevent campaigning.

formation.explanation: Leader proposals receive term/index, append to the log and queue a persistence-delayed self acknowledgment. Peer acknowledgments update progress; tracker aggregates current voters using both majorities for joint configuration, then maybeCommit checks the current log term before advancing commitment. Acknowledgment-driven advancement broadcasts append and releases queued reads, while configuration-driven advancement broadcasts without that release.

context.explanation: Campaign transitions establish candidate term and self vote; vote eligibility uses local vote/leader context and log freshness. PreVote leaves term and vote unchanged. Step handles message terms before role handlers, with explicit pre-vote/lease exceptions and lower-term rejection. Role reset clears accumulated progress and readOnly context while preserving the committed prefix.

connection.explanation: Term dispatch prevents ordinary old responses from becoming new leader support. Persistence-delayed vote/append replies and leader self replies connect durable support to election and commit decisions. Configuration application reinterprets peer progress through a changed voter set and may itself advance commitment; established committed history constrains snapshots and subsequent log repair.

formation.explanation: Leader proposals receive term/index, append to the log and queue a persistence-delayed self acknowledgment. Peer acknowledgments update progress; tracker aggregates current voters using both majorities for joint configuration, then maybeCommit checks the current log term before advancing commitment. Acknowledgment-driven advancement broadcasts append and releases queued reads, while configuration-driven advancement broadcasts without that release. Voter sets use n/2+1 majorities. Followers match the preceding entry, protect committed history and publish durable append responses. Rejection probes, heartbeat recovery and snapshots replenish lagging support. Ready delivers committed entries separately from actual host application.

context.explanation: Campaign transitions establish candidate term and self vote; vote eligibility uses local vote/leader context and log freshness. PreVote leaves term and vote unchanged. Step handles message terms before role handlers, with explicit pre-vote/lease exceptions and lower-term rejection. Role reset clears accumulated progress and readOnly context while preserving the committed prefix. Candidate handlers accept the matching vote response kind, deduplicate votes and tally current voters. Pre-vote success starts an actual campaign; real quorum success elects a leader and appends its no-op. Timer quorum loss and higher terms revoke leadership; transfer waits for target replication and expires. Campaign admission excludes learners, pending snapshots and committed configuration entries above the accounted applied frontier.

connection.explanation: Term dispatch prevents ordinary old responses from becoming new leader support. Persistence-delayed vote/append replies and leader self replies connect durable support to election and commit decisions. Configuration application reinterprets peer progress through a changed voter set and may itself advance commitment; established committed history constrains snapshots and subsequent log repair. Host configuration installation changes voter eligibility separately from application accounting. Restart restores term/vote, committed history and ConfState, while volatile support is rebuilt. Async storage uses FIFO completion and term-stamped append responses; application acknowledgments remain term-independent. Old pre-first-commit read requests can survive a reset, but read quorum acknowledgments do not; any later release uses current committed state and a fresh read round. Synchronous early Advance can account application before external completion, leaving configuration admission timing as a focused unresolved premise.
